editorial:
Imagine being stuck in a small apartment during a massive storm with the people you love but don't really get along with anymore. That is exactly where you find Ryota, a guy who used to be a famous writer but is now just struggling to make ends meet as a private eye. He is divorced from his wife Kyoko and barely sees his son Shingo. When a typhoon hits, they all end up trapped at his mother's place for the night. The vibe is very quiet and cozy, but there is a lot of tension under the surface because everyone is trying to figure out where they fit in each other's lives now.

You will love how the acting feels real, like you are eavesdropping on a real family. The pacing is slow, so if you want explosions or fast action, this isn't for you. However, the small moments of kindness and regret make it hit home. It is a great pick for a rainy Sunday.
endingExplained: At the end, the storm clears and the family has to say goodbye. Ryota has a heart-to-heart talk with his mother and realizes how much he missed out on. He does not magically fix his marriage or become a star writer again, but he finds a sense of peace. He accepts his life as it is and feels closer to his son. It ends with a feeling of hope and new beginnings.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves gentle stories about family and forgiveness.
